text:
Only for your lips my blood is ripe,

with summer obsession

prepared for your kisses,

always faithful to my arms and full of

beauty,

bloodless every night, and each dawn unharmed.


If the woods crackle with hunting and adventure

and the high birds

mock seeing us imprisoned,

do not let your eyes draw the bitterness

of those who have not carried love in their bones.


Stay in my arms, for you have only me,

for the others

hate you, for the heart lies in wait for you

in the warm beats of belly

and temples.


See that there are no gardens beyond this wall,

that it is all a

long forgetting. and if my love tightens around you

you will see an open sky behind

the dark weeping.


1968

translation.title: Tigers in the Garden
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's tense enclosure, bodily pulse, and the promise of sky behind dark weeping.
